baseline_models.mechanism: Withholding is repeated as both conduct and commanded content: a private refusal of rightful release becomes a norm imposed on a human collective and thereby reproduces itself socially.

activation_trace.role: Withholding possessions from those for whom they should not be retained supplies both the practiced act and the policy being propagated.
Demand and obligation convert personal retention into a directive laid upon others.
The visible human collective is the field across which the withholding norm is made public and transmissible.

changed_reading.before: Certain people are stingy and tell others to be stingy.
changed_reading.after: The verse diagnoses a self-reproducing social order: retainers turn blocked claims into a command for the wider human group.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
baseline_models.mechanism: Turning away is relational withdrawal, but the closing names a sufficiency and praiseworthiness that do not depend on the withdrawing party; refusal ruptures human participation without creating lack or diminished worth in God.

activation_trace.role: Withdrawal and aversion supply the human movement away from proximity, hearing, and compliance.
Freedom from need blocks any inference that human withholding deprives God of a required resource.
Abundant praiseworthy qualities make divine worth intrinsic rather than conferred by human compliance.

changed_reading.before: Whoever refuses is warned that God needs nothing.
changed_reading.after: Turning away is exposed as self-exclusion: neither retained goods nor withheld allegiance can reduce divine sufficiency or praiseworthiness.

baseline_models.mechanism: The authority branches of command and taking charge permit a political reading: withholding does not remain an appetite but captures an office, positioning its practitioners as arbiters of what the public should release.

activation_trace.role: Improper retention supplies the substantive rule promoted by the would-be arbiters.
Rule, office, and authority widen the verbal command into an exploratory claim about control of allocation.
Taking charge of an affair keeps governance live beside the surface sense of turning away.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, miserliness seeks jurisdiction: it occupies the social office from which distributions and duties are defined.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surrounding economy treats resources as something sent out by temporary successors and ultimately inherited by God. Bukhul therefore becomes a custody failure: provisional holders act as final owners and stop what was entrusted from reaching its claims.

activation_trace.role: Improper retention is recast as the custodian's blockage of goods that carry claims beyond the holder.
Divine lacklessness makes expenditure a duty of custody rather than revenue supplied to a needy recipient.
The going-out of property in expenditure supplies the release that bukhul blocks.
One holder coming after another and standing in a predecessor's place makes possession successive rather than absolute.
Inheritance as transfer from predecessor to heir gives the horizon in which all holdings finally revert beyond present possessors.

structural_cues: 57:7 places expenditure beside being made successors over what is held, while 57:10 places refusal to spend beside God's inheritance of the heavens and earth.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies expenditure, successive holding, and final inheritance; I infer that succession limits title and turns bukhul into failed custody. A live alternative is that succession marks agency without implying a formal trust relation.

changed_reading.before: Bukhul is an owner's excessive reluctance to part with personal property.
changed_reading.after: Bukhul is a temporary holder's false claim to final ownership, blocking the release required by delegated custody.

context_deltas.mechanism: The loan passages model giving as cutting a portion away so that recompense returns multiplied, and they name charitable actors through a truth-and-solidness root. Bukhul becomes refusal to let possession enter a morally guaranteed circuit, not merely preference for a larger balance.

activation_trace.role: Retention supplies the closed stock that resists being cut loose for another's claim.
Sufficiency and adequacy prevent the loan metaphor from implying that God needs financing.
Cutting away property or work for returned recompense supplies the circuit's release-and-return structure.
Increase by a matching multiple makes release generative rather than simple depletion.
The wealth-charity branch identifies the men and women who enact the open alternative to retention.

structural_cues: 57:11 and 57:18 repeat the good-loan and multiplication construction before 57:24 repeats bukhul as act and commanded noun.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies severance for recompense, multiplication, and charitable actors; I infer a circulation model in which bukhul closes the loop before release. Alternatively, the loan wording may function only as reward assurance without implying circulation.

changed_reading.before: The miser fears that giving simply subtracts from what is held.
changed_reading.after: The miser refuses the first cut in a release-return circuit whose multiplication contests the premise that giving is terminal loss.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding instruction regulates distress over what escapes and exultation over what arrives, then names conceited boasting before 57:24 opens with a plural relative. This makes bukhul the distributive behavior of an affective possession system organized around loss, acquisition, display, and status.

activation_trace.role: Withholding rightful release becomes the behavioral output of attachment to possession and rank.
Failure to reach or retain what escapes supplies the loss-pole around which possessiveness contracts.
Exultant arrogance supplies the acquisition-pole that turns receipt into self-inflation.
Conceit displayed in bearing connects possession to a socially visible posture.
Counting and boasting over accumulated distinction gives withholding a status-preserving payoff.

structural_cues: 57:24's opening الَّذِينَ can continue the immediately preceding plural characterization of every conceited boaster in 57:23.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, a plural relative opening, loss, exultation, conceit, and boasting; I infer both a syntactic continuation and a psychological arrow from possessive affect to withholding. The live alternative is that الَّذِينَ begins a looser new class rather than a restrictive continuation.

changed_reading.before: Bukhul is a discrete financial vice.
changed_reading.after: Bukhul is the public allocation behavior of a larger affective system that panics at loss, swells at receipt, and converts holdings into displayed rank.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same human public commanded toward bukhul in 57:24 is next summoned to rise through book and balance in equity. The focus command is therefore a counter-institution: it trains the public away from measured claims and toward normalized blockage.

activation_trace.role: Obligating speech supplies the rival norm that organizes public conduct.
Improper retention is the counter-command's substantive rule.
The balance of justice supplies a public standard against which blocked claims can be measured.
Rising with resolve to an affair makes equity an enacted social undertaking rather than an abstract value.
The same visible human collective becomes the subject of justice and beneficiary of material usefulness.
Equity and fair dealing state the social direction opposed to commanded withholding.

structural_cues: 57:24 and 57:25 are adjacent and repeat النَّاس across opposed constructions: commanding people toward bukhul and enabling people to rise in qist.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated people, command, balance, rising, and equity; I infer that the two adjacent directions are institutional rivals. A live alternative is that 57:25 states the general mission of messengers without serving as a direct answer to 57:24.

changed_reading.before: Ordering stinginess is interpersonal moral corruption.
changed_reading.after: Ordering stinginess is an anti-justice institution that diverts the same public from standing up measured claims.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing declaration locates bounty in God's owning hand and its delivery in God's giving. Human bukhul and its social enforcement become attempted gatekeeping of a surplus whose source, custody, and destination they do not control.

activation_trace.role: Withholding from rightful destinations supplies the attempted human gate.
Divine independence makes bounty originate in abundance rather than in a need serviced by gatekeepers.
Bounty as benefaction and gift identifies what no human group can monopolize.
The owning hand fixes real control of bounty outside the human retainers who claim allocation power.
Active giving supplies the outward movement that defeats attempted enclosure.

structural_cues: The surah closes by repeating divine bounty three times and denying a community control over any of it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies gift, owning hand, and giving; I infer that commanding bukhul is an attempted gatekeeping claim over divine surplus. Alternatively, 57:29 may concern communal privilege more narrowly than material allocation.

changed_reading.before: Misers control their own stock and influence others' private choices.
changed_reading.after: Misers pose as gatekeepers of bounty, but the verse's divine names and the surah's close deny them ownership of either its source or distribution.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening locates sovereignty with God and says affairs return to God. Against that frame, commanding people to retain becomes a local counterfeit of jurisdiction: an allocation policy issued inside a dominion the issuers neither own nor finally administer.

activation_trace.role: Authority and office keep the misers' command legible as a jurisdictional claim.
Taking charge of an affair supplies the governance field from which withdrawal or usurpation can occur.
Sovereignty fixes the encompassing domain in which human allocation commands remain subordinate.
Affairs and public matters returning to God deny finality to the misers' asserted rule.

structural_cues: 57:2 and 57:5 repeat divine sovereignty near the opening; 57:5 also sends all affairs back to God before 57:24 depicts human commanders.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine sovereignty, returning affairs, and the focus's command/office branches; I infer a hierarchy of jurisdictions in which bukhul is counterfeit rule. The alternative is to keep يأمرون at ordinary exhortation with no office-level implication.

changed_reading.before: The speakers have bad influence over peers.
changed_reading.after: Their influence mimics jurisdiction, issuing an allocation rule inside property and affairs that ultimately belong and return elsewhere.

context_deltas.mechanism: The world-life sequence takes accumulated wealth through a plant-like cycle into broken debris. Retention thus appears as an anti-temporal project: trying to immobilize as permanent stock matter whose disclosed trajectory is fragmentation.

activation_trace.role: Holding possessions back supplies the attempted freezing of material flow.
Enduring lacklessness contrasts with the contingent stock that the miser tries to preserve.
Acquiring and multiplying wealth supplies the stock around which competitive retention forms.
The world's vanishing debris supplies the terminal material state that defeats permanent enclosure.

structural_cues: 57:20 embeds wealth and children inside a growth, yellowing, and debris sequence shortly before the focus verse.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies accumulated wealth and a material cycle ending in debris; I infer that bukhul attempts to stop that temporal flow. Alternatively, the cycle may warn only against worldly valuation rather than characterize withholding itself.

changed_reading.before: Bukhul preserves a finite stock against depletion.
changed_reading.after: Bukhul futilely tries to freeze transient matter, confusing an eventual debris-state with enduring sufficiency.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because 57:27 concerns invented monasticism, not explicit avarice. It remains anchored in 57:24's command to withhold and is activated by fear-based devotion, invention, prescription, and failed observance. Downstream prose should present it only as a possible critique of pious-seeming, human-authored austerity regimes, not as an equation of monasticism or restraint with bukhul.

activation_trace.role: Withholding what should not be retained anchors austerity only where it blocks a rightful claim.
Imposed demand anchors the reading in a social rule of restraint rather than private renunciation.
Devotion generated by fear supplies the pious appearance of the austerity regime.
Initiation without a prior model supplies the regime's human-authored novelty.
An inscription that imposes judgment distinguishes what was prescribed from what people imposed.
Attentive observance and supervision expose the failure to care properly for the instituted practice.

changed_reading.before: The verse condemns affluent people who promote ordinary stinginess.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it can also expose pious-seeming authorities who universalize an invented austerity that withholds rightful goods and then fails its own duty of care.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This material analogy is surprising because the ش د د occurrence in 57:25 modifies might, while the cited branch image names severity of bukhul, and iron is not itself condemned. It remains anchored in the focus's repeated bukhul and in 57:25's sequence of hardness and public benefits. Downstream prose should mark the contrast as branch-distant: useful hardness releases benefit under justice, whereas miserly hardness traps it.

activation_trace.role: Improper retention anchors the analogy in a hardness that refuses outward benefit.
Iron and resistant solidity supply the material hardness whose function can be publicly directed.
The branch image of severe bukhul makes constrictive hardness echo across the adjacent verses.
Benefit opposed to harm supplies the outward social yield that distinguishes useful strength from retention.

changed_reading.before: Bukhul is merely the absence of generosity.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, bukhul is misdirected hardness: unlike iron mobilized for justice and benefit, it hardens around goods so their usefulness cannot pass outward.

strongest_changes: Successorship and inheritance revise bukhul from excessive ownership into failed custody by a temporary holder.
The adjacency to 57:23 makes withholding the distributive behavior of loss-anxiety, exultation, conceit, and boasting.
The repeated human public in 57:24-25 turns commanded bukhul into a counter-institution opposed to standing in measured equity.
The final location of bounty in God's owning and giving hand denies human retainers any real gatekeeping jurisdiction.
summary.what_was_special: The focus verse is a hinge where a private act becomes public command: earlier spending, succession, lending, and impermanence explain what is being blocked, while later balance, equity, and divine bounty expose that blockage as rival social governance rather than isolated stinginess.
remaining_uncertainties: The syntactic force of الَّذِينَ after 57:23 may be tight continuation or looser resumption.
The office and jurisdiction branches of ء م ر and و ل ي are live but form-distant from the most immediate verbal senses.
The austerity and material-hardness outliers require explicit qualification and should not displace the strong economic-social reading.
